77:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Mursalat Al-Bukhari said: Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Al-A’mash narrated to us, Ibrahim narrated to me, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah - he is Ibn Mas’ud - may God be pleased with him, who said: “While we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a cave in Mina, the verse ‘By the Messengers’ was revealed to him. He was reciting it, and I was receiving it from his mouth, and his mouth was wet with it. Then a snake jumped on us. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Kill it.’ So we rushed to it, and it went away. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I have been protected from your evil as you have been protected from its evil.’” Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Al-A’mash. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubaydullah, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, on the authority of his mother, that she heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite Al-Mursalat in arruff in the Maghrib prayer. In the narration of Malik, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubaydullah, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, that Umm Al-Fadl heard him recite ‘By the Messengers’ in arruff, and she said: ‘O my son, your recitation of this surah reminds me of it. It is the last thing I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite in the Maghrib prayer.’” It was narrated by both of them in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim on the authority of Malik. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Zakariya bin Sahl al-Marwazi told us, Ali bin al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us, al-Husayn bin Waqid told us, al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, And those sent forth in gusts he said: The angels. And it was narrated on the authority of Masruq, Abu al-Dhaha, and Mujahid in one of the narrations, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi’ bin Anas something similar to that. And it was narrated on the authority of Abu Salih that he said: They are the messengers, and in a narration on his authority that they are the angels. And this is what Abu Salih said about al-Asifat, al-Nashirat, al-Farqat, and al-Mulqiyyat that they are the angels. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl on the authority of Muslim al-Batin on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn who said: I asked Ibn Masoud about al-Mursalat in arruff. He said: It is the wind. He also said this about al-‘Aseefat a gushan, and al-Nashirat Nashraan that it is the wind. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Abu Salih said this in one narration from him. Ibn Jarir hesitated regarding al-Mursalat in arruff - is it the angels when they are sent in a gushan or like the mane of horses following one another, or is it the wind when it blows little by little? He was definitive that al-‘Aseefat a gushan is the wind as Ibn Masoud and those who followed him said. Among those who said this about al-‘Aseefat a gushan were also Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-Suddi. He hesitated regarding al-Nashirat Nashraan - is it the angels or the wind as mentioned above? On the authority of Abu Saleh, the Nashirat Nashrān is the rain, and it is more apparent that the Mursalāt are the winds, as God Almighty said: And We sent the fertilizing winds and God Almighty said: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy and thus the Asifāt are the winds. It is said that the winds blew with a sound, and similarly the Nashirat are the winds that spread the clouds in the horizons of the sky as the Lord Almighty wills. God the Almighty said: {And those who distinguish, and those who cast down the Reminder, as an excuse or a warning} meaning the angels. This was stated by Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn `Abbas, Masruq, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ar-Rabi` ibn Anas, As-Suddi and Ath-Thawri. There is no disagreement here, for they descend by God’s command to the messengers, distinguishing between truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, lawful and unlawful, and they deliver to the messengers a revelation in which there is an excuse for creation and a warning to them of God’s punishment if they disobey His command. God the Almighty said: {Indeed, what you are promised will surely come to pass} This is what is sworn by with these oaths, that is, what you have been promised of the establishment of the Hour, the blowing of the Trumpet, the resurrection of bodies, the gathering of the first and the last on one plain, and the recompense of every doer for his deeds, whether good or evil. All of this will surely come to pass, meaning it will inevitably occur. Then the Almighty said: Then when the stars are extinguished, meaning their light is gone, as in the Almighty’s saying: And when the stars are scattered, and as in the Almighty’s saying: And when the stars are scattered, “And when the sky is split open,” meaning it is cracked and split, its edges are drooped, and its extremities are weakened. And when the mountains are blown away means they are taken away, leaving no trace or trace of them, as in the saying of God the Almighty: “And they ask you, [O Muhammad], about the mountains. Say, ‘My Lord will blow them away with a blast’” (Al-Baqarah 2:17). And God the Almighty said: And the Day We set the mountains in motion and you see the earth barren, and We gather them together and will not leave behind a single one of them (Al-Baqarah 2:17). Ath-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Ibrahim: gathered means threatened, and it is as if he makes it like His saying the Almighty: “And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Book will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forth, and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged” (Al-Baqarah 2:17). 77:29: God Almighty says, informing us about the unbelievers who deny the Resurrection, the Recompense, Paradise, and Hellfire, that it will be said to them on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:“Go to that which you used to deny. Go to a shade with three branches.” That is, the flame of Hell when it rises and smoke ascends with it, and because of its intensity and strength, it has three branches. It neither provides shade nor protects against the flame. That is, the shade of smoke opposite the flame does not provide shade in itself, nor does it protect against the flame, that is, it does not protect them from the heat of the flame. And the Almighty said: It throws out sparks like castles. That is, the sparks fly from its flame like castles. Ibn Mas’ud said: Like fortresses. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam and others: meaning the roots of trees. As if they were yellow camels. That is, like black camels. Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak said this, and Ibn Jarir chose it. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Sa’id ibn Jubayr: Yellow camels means the ropes of ships. And on his authority, I mean Ibn Abbas: Yellow camels are pieces of copper. Al-Bukhari said: Amr ibn Ali told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abis, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, It throws out sparks like castles. He said: We used to take a piece of wood three cubits high or more, and raise it up to build, and we would call it a castle. As if they were yellow camels. The ropes of ships were gathered until they were like the waists of men. Woe, that Day, to the deniers. Then the Almighty said: This is a Day on which they will not speak. That is, they will not speak. Nor… They will be given permission to apologize.” That is, they will not be able to speak, nor will they be given permission to apologize. Rather, the proof has been established against them, and the word has been pronounced against them for what they did wrong, so they will not speak. The stages of the Resurrection will be states, and the Lord Almighty will tell of this state sometimes and of that state sometimes, to indicate the severity of the terrors and earthquakes on that day. For this reason, He will say after each section of this speech: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. God the Almighty says: “This is the Day of Judgment. We have gathered you and the former peoples. * So if you have a plan, then plot.” This is the Creator addressing His servants, saying to them: “This is the Day of Judgment. We have gathered you and the former peoples.” Meaning that He has gathered them with His power on a single plain where they can hear the caller and see clearly. God the Almighty’s saying: But if you have a plan, then plot. This is a severe threat and a firm warning, meaning that if you are able to escape My grasp and escape My judgment, then do so, for you will not be able to do so, as God the Almighty says: “O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except by authority.” God the Almighty also says: and you will not harm Him at all. In the hadith: O My servants, you will never be able to benefit Me so as to benefit Me, and you will never be able to harm Me so as to harm Me. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Mundhir Al-Tariqi Al-Awdi narrated to us, Muhammad bin Fadil narrated to us, Husayn bin Abd Al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of Hassan bin Abi Al-Mukhariq, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Al-Jadali, who said: I came to Jerusalem and found Ubadah bin Al-Samit, Abdullah bin Amr, and Kaab Al-Ahbar talking in Jerusalem. Ubadah said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will gather the first and the last on one plain, so that the sight will pierce them and the caller will hear them, and God will say: “This is the Day of Judgment. We have gathered you and the former peoples. So if you have a plan, then plan it.” Today no stubborn tyrant will escape from Me, nor a rebellious devil. Abdullah bin Amr said: We will tell you on that day that a neck will emerge from the Fire and set out, until when it is among the people, it will call out: O people, I have been sent to three whom I know better than a father knows his son, and a brother knows his brother. No sin will elude me, and nothing will conceal them from me: the one who made another god with God, and every stubborn tyrant and every rebellious devil. Then it will wrap itself around them and throw them into the Fire before… The account is forty years old.

77:41: The Almighty says, informing about His righteous servants who worshipped Him by performing the obligatory duties and avoiding the forbidden things, that on the Day of Resurrection they will be in gardens and springs, in contrast to the shade of the black, stinking smoke that those wretched ones will be in. And the Almighty says: And fruits of whatever they desire, meaning, from all kinds of fruits, whatever they seek, they will find. Eat and drink in happiness for what you used to do, meaning, this will be said to them as a way of being kind to them. Then the Almighty says, informing them in a new, renewed way: Thus do We reward the doers of good, meaning, this is Our reward for those who do good deeds. Woe, that Day, to the deniers. And the Almighty’s saying: Eat and enjoy yourselves a little, for indeed, you are criminals is addressed to those who deny the Day of Judgment, and their command is a threat and warning. Woe, that Day, to the deniers as the Almighty said: We will give them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a severe punishment and the Almighty said: “Indeed, those who invent falsehood against God will not succeed. Enjoyment in this world, then to Us is their return. Then We will make them taste the severe punishment for what they used to disbelieve” and the Almighty’s saying: And when it is said to them, ‘Bow down,’ they do not bow down meaning when these ignorant disbelievers are commanded to be among the congregational worshippers, they will refuse to do so and be arrogant about it. For this reason the Almighty said: Woe, that Day, to the deniers then the Almighty said: Then in what statement after this will they believe? Then let him say: I believe in God and in what He revealed. This hadith was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Qiyamah. The end of the interpretation of Surat Al-Mursalat. Praise and gratitude be to God, and to Him belongs success and protection.
